findings.description: Content contains Unicode characters visually identical to ASCII (math alphanumerics, Cyrillic/Greek lookalikes) appearing near ASCII text, which may indicate a homoglyph attack
findings.remediation: Replace confusable Unicode characters with their ASCII equivalents.
findings.title: Confusable Unicode characters in text

findings.description: Hostname 'іnstall.example-clі.dev' contains non-ASCII characters which may be a homograph attack
findings.remediation: Verify the domain is the intended target. Compare the raw hostname bytes against the expected ASCII domain.
findings.title: Non-ASCII characters in hostname

findings.description: Label 'іnstall' mixes multiple Unicode scripts ({Cyrillic, Latin}), potential homograph
findings.remediation: Inspect the hostname character by character. Use tirith diff <url> to see the raw vs parsed hostname.
findings.title: Mixed scripts in hostname label

findings.description: Domain contains punycode label 'xn--nstall-ovf' which may disguise the actual domain
findings.remediation: Decode the punycode label to see the actual Unicode characters and verify the domain is legitimate.
findings.title: Punycode domain detected

findings.description: Domain uses '.dev' TLD which can be confused with file extensions
findings.remediation: Verify the domain is legitimate and not impersonating a file download.
findings.title: Lookalike TLD detected

findings.description:
Command pipes output from 'curl' directly to interpreter 'bash'. Downloaded content will be executed without inspection.
  Safer: run `tirith check --suggest -- <command>`; Tirith emits a typed capsule command only when it can prove the URL, interpreter, argv, and stdin semantics. Otherwise download into a private location (or use `vet <url>`, https://getvet.sh) and review the exact bytes before execution.
findings.remediation: Run tirith check --suggest on the exact original command. On x86_64 Linux, use an emitted absolute --script-stdin/--interpreter capsule command only when Tirith is root-managed and curl supplied both -f/--fail and -L/--location semantics; the runner will fail closed unless the interpreter's first PATH hit is also root-managed. Other architectures, platforms, install paths, and unsupported command shapes remain guidance-only and require manual review.
findings.title: Pipe to interpreter: curl | bash
